prompt.title: Testcontainers integration tests, ArchUnit fences and legacy refactoring

var.name: target_architecture
var.example: hexagonal: domain, application, adapter; adapters depend inward only

variables.var: where the code should end up

var.name: known_behaviour
var.example: Production quirks: cancelling a SHIPPED order returns 200 and does nothing; totals round HALF_UP

variables.var: behaviour that must be preserved, including the odd parts

context.platform: Spring Boot 4.1.2 managed Testcontainers 2.0.5 (modules such as testcontainers-postgresql and testcontainers-kafka), @ServiceConnection, JUnit 6.0.3, ArchUnit 1.5.1.

instructions.step: Write characterization tests before changing anything: drive the legacy entry points against real PostgreSQL and Kafka in Testcontainers and record current outputs as approved snapshots, quirks included.
Write the target architecture as ArchUnit rules over {{root_package}}, then wrap them in FreezingArchRule.freeze so today's violations are recorded and only new ones fail.

Refactor in small steps (extract a pure function, introduce a port, move a class); after each step run the characterization tests and the ArchUnit tests, and remove frozen violations as they are fixed.
Where a quirk must change, change it in a separate commit with its own test and a note for the owners.
Report each step with its test results and the frozen-violation count.

invariants.inv: Characterization tests exist and pass on the unchanged code before the first refactoring commit.
Every refactoring commit keeps all characterization tests green; behaviour changes are separate commits.
ArchUnit rules encode the target architecture and run frozen; the stored violation count never increases.
Integration tests use real PostgreSQL and Kafka containers through @ServiceConnection, never H2 or mocks of the database.
Each container image is pinned to a version tag.

anti_goals.no: No big-bang rewrite and no refactoring before the characterization tests are green.
No deleting or editing the frozen-violation store by hand to make a build pass.
No snapshot updates without a line in the report saying which behaviour changed and why.

output_contract.report: Per step: what moved, tests run and their results, frozen violations before and after.

verification.check: The first commit adds only tests, and they pass.
The report lists every commit with its characterization result.
The store diff only removes lines across the refactoring.
grep finds no H2 dependency and no mocked DataSource in integration tests.
Every container constructor uses a tagged image name.

prompt.task: Characterize, fence and incrementally refactor the legacy code toward the target architecture, honouring every invariant.
